subject: dik-dik antelope
title: This Antelope Lives in Dry African Bush and Never Needs to Drink

scenes.text: This antelope lives in hot, dry African bush, and it doesn't need to drink.
The dik-dik weighs three to six kilos, about the size of a small dog.
It gets all the water it needs from the leaves, shoots and fruit it eats.
And it stays cool with its odd, stretched nose. Muscles pump blood through it like bellows.
When it's very hot, it pants through that nose, and evaporation cools its blood.
Its name even comes from its nose: the whistling alarm call sounds like dik-dik.

description:
Kirk's dik-dik, a tiny antelope of East African bush, is water-independent: it gets the water it needs from the plants it eats.
Its elongated snout works like a radiator: when it is very hot it pants through the nose and evaporation cools the blood. Its name comes from the female's alarm call.
What other animal survives without drinking?
first_comment: Dik-diks pair up for life and spend about two thirds of their time together. What tiny animal should we cover next?
